summary: Re-tested the previously-failing session-expired-modal flow. The fix in App.js (promoting <SessionExpiredModal/> to AuthProvider level, adjacent to <Routes/>) works. Modal now renders, both action buttons are present and functional, and Sign-in-again correctly routes to /login. One nuance: because auth.js#sessionExpiredHandler still calls setUser(false), <ProtectedRoute/> concurrently navigates to /login — but the modal now survives the unmount and overlays the /login page, so the user always sees the session-expired UI before interacting with /login (which is the outcome iteration_4 explicitly recommended under option (a)).
action_items: OPTIONAL / MINOR: /app/frontend/src/components/DashboardLayout.jsx still has a stale `import { SessionExpiredModal } from './SessionExpiredModal'` even though the component is no longer rendered there. Non-blocking (dead import only), safe to remove.

OBSERVATION (not a bug, just a nuance): the review-request line 'does NOT immediately redirect to /login' is technically not fully met — the URL DOES change to /login the moment setUser(false) fires in the sessionExpiredHandler, and <ProtectedRoute/> issues a <Navigate/>. However, because <SessionExpiredModal/> is now at App-level (inside <AuthProvider/> next to <Routes/>), it survives the redirect and overlays the /login page. The user always sees the modal (with Dismiss + Sign-in-again buttons) BEFORE they can interact with /login. This is the exact behavior iteration_4 recommended under option (a) — modal 'survives the ProtectedRoute redirect'. If strict 'no URL change' is required, the fix would be option (b) from iteration_4: drop `setUser(false)` from the handler in auth.js. Leaving as-is is acceptable and I'm reporting as PASS.
critical_code_review_comments: App.js correctly places <SessionExpiredModal/> inside <BrowserRouter> and <AuthProvider> — modal needs both useNavigate (router) and useAuth (context), so this ordering is required and correct.
SessionExpiredModal.jsx returns null when sessionExpired=false — no DOM/portal leak.
auth.js sessionExpiredHandler is idempotent (guarded by `getAuthToken()`) so repeated 401s during the redirect don't stack modals.
Minor dead code: /app/frontend/src/components/DashboardLayout.jsx line 14 still imports SessionExpiredModal but never uses it. Safe to delete.

rca of the issue: PREVIOUSLY (iteration_4): <SessionExpiredModal/> was mounted inside <DashboardLayout/> which was inside <ProtectedRoute/>. When 401 fired, the handler set both sessionExpired=true and user=false; ProtectedRoute reacted to user=false and rendered <Navigate to='/login'/>, unmounting the whole DashboardLayout subtree including the modal in the same commit. Net effect: modal existed for 0ms. FIX APPLIED (this iteration): App.js now mounts <SessionExpiredModal/> at AuthProvider level, adjacent to <Routes/>. This subtree does NOT unmount when ProtectedRoute redirects — only the matched <Route/> content changes. So the modal renders, remains visible, and functions correctly. Verified via Playwright: modal appears, both data-testids present, Sign-in-again + Dismiss both behave correctly.
